Design Principles
  • Make the structure and interaction obvious
  • Use strong type and borders with a clear hierarchy
  • Choose a limited high-contrast palette
  • Let hard shadows describe layers consistently
  • Keep intentional irregularity separate from accidental disorder

When to use it

  • Creative studio or portfolio
    Stop overthinking. Ship it.An indie developer’s defiance and directness
  • Youth, culture, and event campaigns

When NOT to use it

  • Use constant visual shouting in a dense work tool
    Banking app (thick black outlines + fluorescent pink)Finance and healthcare need trust; a brutalist treatment can feel unreliable.
  • Sacrifice reading and focus states for attitude
    Enterprise tools need credibility, scanability, and clear states first.
  • Mix many unrelated colors, borders, and shadows
    Government service portal (high-contrast palette)Formal service contexts should prioritize dignity, stability, and ease of use.
  • Imitate roughness without a consistent layout

Solid black stroke 2-3px hard shadow Highly saturated contrasting colors Aa900 bold black title Press displacement
Create paper-cut outlines with uniform scale, and adjust color and thickness according to theme and component size
Non-blurred solid color displacement creates a collage feel, and the offset is set according to space and control size.
Examples use fluorescent powder, bright yellow and bright blue; the actual color palette must have primary and secondary colors and pass comparison tests
Large bold fonts establish visual attitude. Chinese and English need to deal with font weight, font spacing and line breaks separately.
Feedback must be provided on hover, focus and pressed states, not just the mouse.
AI Prompt

Neo-brutalist creator dashboard, clear income and order hierarchy, 2–3px black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, yellow base with limited pink and blue status accents, extreme 800/400 type-weight contrast

# Neo-Brutalism

You might say
Go bold and expressive with thick black borders, bright color blocks, and hard shadows.

**Use direct structure, strong contrast, and deliberately exposed construction**·Neo-brutalist web design uses heavy outlines, bold type, simple shapes, hard shadows, and obvious interaction. It can feel energetic and candid when the hierarchy remains disciplined. Random misalignment and aggressive color do not become a design system just because they look unconventional.

Scroll sideways to explore the full example

Design Principles

- Make the structure and interaction obvious
- Use strong type and borders with a clear hierarchy
- Choose a limited high-contrast palette
- Let hard shadows describe layers consistently
- Keep intentional irregularity separate from accidental disorder

### When to use it

- Creative studio or portfolio

Stop overthinking. Ship it.An indie developer’s defiance and directness
- Youth, culture, and event campaigns

E-book ¥29Gumroad-style digital goods
- A product with a direct, playful voice

Hackathon 202648 hours
- Small sites that benefit from strong identity

“Anti-polish” is a stance too

### When NOT to use it

- Use constant visual shouting in a dense work tool

Banking app (thick black outlines + fluorescent pink)Finance and healthcare need trust; a brutalist treatment can feel unreliable.
- Sacrifice reading and focus states for attitude

Enterprise tools need credibility, scanability, and clear states first.
- Mix many unrelated colors, borders, and shadows

Government service portal (high-contrast palette)Formal service contexts should prioritize dignity, stability, and ease of use.
- Imitate roughness without a consistent layout
